name: DCGAN (CIFAR-10)

rebuild.time: 26m41s traced (24m57s of it the CIFAR-10 download; 1m42s of training)
rebuild.hw: 1x Tesla T4, 4 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL, CUDA 13.0 (as recorded in the DAG runtime; the instance type itself is not in the record)
rebuild.costNote: Capture cost was lost with the operator's working directory and is deliberately not estimated. The tier-2 certification cost ~$0.41 per the campaign ledger. See costs.md.

patch.summary: +110/-0 across 6 files, none of them Python. dcgan/main.py is byte-for-byte upstream. The diff is a treqs workflow, a treqs config, two .gitkeep files, and a .gitignore change that converts upstream's directory-ignores on the output paths into contents-ignores so the directories survive a clean checkout and their artifacts become lineage edges.

truncationNote: 1 epoch of an upstream default 25 (782 iterations at batch 64 over CIFAR-10's 50,000 training images). Reproduce, not replicate - no convergence and no sample-quality claim. The truncation is also stated in the artifact's own roar put message and label description, so it travels with the model.

certification.exitCodeSource: roar's own job DB, not a parsed banner
certification.stepsNote: The DAG has 3 jobs; the third is the roar put, excluded by --no-puts by design. 2/2 is the whole reproducible pipeline.
certification.manifestDiff: 45/45 recorded pip pins present at exact recorded versions (0 missing, 0 mismatched); both steps then ran to exit 0 with no ModuleNotFoundError, demonstrating the recorded set is sufficient for this row's import graph and not merely resolvable
certification.outputsNote: Byte-identical output is NOT claimed and was not observed. fake_samples_epoch_000.png is a PNG of generated images, so its compressed size tracks pixel content and GPU training is not bit-deterministic at a fixed seed. The two size-invariant files (a fixed-shape state dict, and a grid of dataset images chosen deterministically by the seed) matched exactly. A fourth recorded output, netD_epoch_0.pth (11,076,841 B at capture), was not stat'd on the rebuild host.
certification.attempts: First success after 3 inconclusive attempts; the campaign ledger records all three as substrate failures rather than row defects.
certification.bareCorePythonFinding: This row settled the campaign's open bare-`python` question. The certification host had no bare `python` on its system PATH, yet the recorded command `python dcgan/main.py ...` ran and exited 0 - so roar reproduce demonstrably activates the uv-provisioned venv for the workload rather than falling through to a host interpreter.
certification.spendSource: campaign ledger figure, not a metered invoice line
certification.evidenceProvenance: RECONSTRUCTED from the campaign ledger's copy of the certifier's report. The certifying operator's working directory was cleaned up before the rule requiring cert evidence on a certs/ branch existed. Nothing was re-run.
certification.freezeCaveat: Captured on roar 0.4.3 (per the record's own roar_version and the roar-cli==0.4.3 pin in the freeze) and certified on 0.4.4.dev0 @ c5c553b - both predate roar #274, a fix to how the freeze pass enumerates installed packages, so this record may be missing packages a later capture would have caught. The imports-vs-freeze audit finds NO decisive miss (everything import torch/torchvision demonstrably loads is present) but three packages that often accompany a torch install are absent: requests, urllib3, charset-normalizer. This workload plausibly never imports them - no networking in the training loop, and torchvision's CIFAR-10 download uses stdlib urllib rather than requests. Weak evidence, NOT a proven defect; and 'no detected miss' is never 'verified complete'.

tier1Recheck.detail: Re-run while reconstructing these notes: clean-dag 13/13, AI-BOM 100/100 (profile Advanced), public-urls ALL PUBLIC, freeze PORTABLE. Nothing has drifted since certification.

reconstructionNote: These notes were reconstructed from the published DAG and the campaign ledger after the operator's original working notes were lost - the working directory was cleaned up before the campaign adopted the rule that notes must be pushed to a per-row branch. summary: DCGAN (Radford et al. 2015) from pytorch/examples, trained on CIFAR-10 for one epoch of a default 25 and published with a complete, publicly resolvable lineage record (AI-BOM 100/100). Zero upstream source lines were changed - dcgan/main.py is byte-for-byte upstream and the entire +110/-0 fork diff is workflow, config and a .gitignore fix. Certified by an independent cold rebuild: exit 0, 2/2 steps, all 45 recorded pins present at their exact recorded versions, and the published 14,323,315 B generator checkpoint regenerated at the same size. Two upstream-facing findings: the repository directory-ignores its output paths, so those directories do not survive a clean checkout and a cold rebuild has nowhere to write; and the CIFAR-10 fetch from cs.toronto.edu is throttled to ~114 kB/s, making the download 94% of the run's wall clock while the GPU sits idle. This row also settled the campaign's bare-`python` question: the certification host had no bare `python` on PATH, yet the recorded `python dcgan/main.py` step ran and exited 0, proving roar reproduce activates the venv it provisions.
